source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani (2025) T-UoT: failure diagnosis on frozen HypoArena cases (appendix D.9)
finding: Gap 2. The T-UoT null result has two causes, not one. Of the 12 largest applied-transform failures, most had a reasonable rule change that was never turned into a competitive hypothesis; a large minority had a bad rule change.
numbers: 7 of 12 failures: reasonable transformation not converted. 5 of 12: weak, misaimed or derailing transformation. Qwen3-14B, 100 tasks, Gemma-3-12B judge.
limits: Only 12 cases hand-sorted by the authors. Same author group as the method. Not code-checked.
agent_relevance: Two checks are needed in O4: gate the edit (is the relaxed rule worth keeping) and force the consequence step. Fixing only propagation leaves about 40 percent of failures.

finding: Gap 2. Simple stage signals do not tell T-UoT wins from losses: the rule edit is applied about as often when T-UoT loses as when it wins, and the edit words are rarely carried into the final answer in either group.
numbers: Gate passed 100% in both groups. Transform applied: 75% in wins vs 83% in non-wins. Rules framing 0.75 vs 0.83. Rules to final-text preservation 0.13 vs 0.16.
limits: Lexical overlap is a crude proxy for propagation. Wins are only 11 of 100 tasks top-ranked.
agent_relevance: Do not measure propagation by word overlap. Use an executable or constraint check on the final answer.

finding: Gap 2. Forcing the model to state one mechanistic consequence of the chosen rule change lifted one frozen failure case from last place to near the top. This is a diagnostic, not a test.
numbers: T-UoT case (ant diversification): delta P(intervened beats original) = +0.25 (0.5 is chance), rank 7 to 2.5, four seeds. The C-UoT sister case: +0.28, rank 4 to 1.5.
limits: One case per mode, hand chosen, intervened by the authors; judge is an LLM. Does not show it generalises.
agent_relevance: Supports adding a derive-one-consequence step to O4, but the larger code-checked test in Gap 2 is still not done.

source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani (2025) T-UoT: plain prompt baseline and backbone dependence (Tables 2, 10)
finding: Gap 1. The plain one-prompt baseline is last on one backbone and first on another, so a scaffold-vs-plain claim depends on the model. No token-matched run is reported.
numbers: Qwen3-14B HypoArena: OnePrompt 1475.7 BTD, 14.3% win rate, last of 7; T-UoT 1484.6 / 17.3%, 6th. GLM-4-9B: OnePrompt 1560.4 / 46.3%, first; E-UoT 1542.1 / 40.7%.
limits: Search methods use many more calls than OnePrompt. The paper does not equalise tokens. Judge is Gemma-3-12B.
agent_relevance: Any O4/O8 test must include the plain prompt and a token-matched best-of-N, and run on at least two backbones.

source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani (2025) T-UoT judge agreement (Tables 11-12, D.3)
finding: Gap 10. LLM judges agree only moderately with each other and with people, and the rule-change contrasts are the least stable. No non-LLM selector was tried.
numbers: Judge pairs Spearman 0.587-0.616 over 700 case-method win shares; hard A/B flips 2.6-5.4%. Contrast T minus ToT: 0.63, 0.51, 0.57 across judge pairs. Human vs Gemini 2.5 Pro (n=27 cells): creativity r=0.708, novelty r=0.224; instance level lower (n=267).
limits: Selection inside T-UoT still uses the LLM (LLMscore, LLMvote). Nobody swapped in execution or a constraint checker.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open. Only a code or constraint check removes the G4/G8 conflict. Treat LLM-judged gains below about 0.05 as noise.

source: Cloos, Barbu, Cueva et al. (2024) Baba Is AI: Break the Rules to Beat the Benchmark
finding: Gap 8. A verifiable rule-change benchmark exists: Baba Is You puzzles in Minigrid where the winning plan needs breaking or making rules (exact-match plan scoring). Models do well on simple tasks and fail when rule operations must be composed in a new order.
numbers: GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Gemini-1.5-Flash; 5 samples per test env, 5 seeds; 10 in-context examples. GPT-4o perfect on the first four distractor settings; all models drop on object-plus-rule distractor; accuracy low for the novel composition break-make-goto (values are in figures and Table 1, not extracted).
quote: Plan: break[wall is stop], make[door is win], goto[door]
limits: 2024 models only. Rules are explicit and finite, so it is closer to combinational than to Boden's transformation. Errors are grounding and path planning, not frame failure.
agent_relevance: Best available code-checked rule-edit test bed for O4. Rerun with current models and scaffolds. Gap 8 partly closed.

source: OMEGA (2025) frontier models, complexity and transformative settings
finding: Gap 3. OMEGA tests prompted frontier models only on complexity scaling and pass@k. The transformative setting is tested only with RL on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. No prompt scaffold or representation hint was tried.
numbers: Frontier models: DeepSeek-R1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, o3-mini, o4-mini, 100 samples per complexity level. Transformative: 7 categories; base accuracy typically below 20%; OOD stays near 0% after RL; only Setting 7 gains +10 pp and only on simple variants. Matrix rank: base 70% OOD fell 30 pp after RL.
limits: Appendix Fig 12 reports frontier results on transformative items only in words (all models struggle with special function intersections and certain polynomial problems).
agent_relevance: Gap 3 stays open. O6 (change representation) on prompted frontier models is untested on OMEGA. The matrix-rank drop warns that training on the familiar tactic entrenches it.

source: Yue et al. (2025) Does RL really incentivize reasoning beyond the base model? (re-read, distillation section)
finding: Gap 4. Under RLVR, pass@1 rises but large-k coverage falls, so RL sharpens. Distillation from a stronger teacher does lift the pass@k curve above the base model. So widening needs new outside content, not self-reward.
numbers: Pass@1 up, pass@256 down for RL models vs base. Different RL algorithms (PPO, GRPO, RLOO, ReMax, DAPO) differ slightly but are not fundamentally different. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B pass@k curve consistently and significantly above base and RL models.
quote: distillation can transfer new reasoning patterns from a stronger teacher
limits: Studied RL training, not inference-time scaffolds. Does not test a rule-change prompt.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open for scaffolds. Prediction: a scaffold that only reselects within the model's own samples cannot beat base pass@k; the test is scaffold pass@1 vs base pass@k at equal samples.

source: Schaeffer, Miranda, Kazdan, Chudnovsky, Koyejo (2026) How Strong Is the Evidence for the Artificial Hivemind?
finding: Gap 5. A conceptual replication with 15 current models and 12 topics: the flagship two-cluster claim fails, the null used was too weak, and the training-level-fix conclusion does not follow. A residual same-prompt convergence effect survives the stronger null.
numbers: Time metaphor: one dominant vehicle in 80.5% of 750 responses plus a long tail; every topic shows more than two clusters; time is least diverse of 12 topics. Same-prompt pairs exceed 0.8 cosine about 2-3 times as often as different-idea pairs. Min-p original claim: 81% of pairs above 0.7, 61.2% above 0.8.
limits: Preprint, one author group, current models not the original 25. No human baseline. Embedding diversity is not human-valued creativity.
agent_relevance: A matched null now exists. Hivemind homogeneity is real but smaller than claimed. Use same-prompt different-idea pairs as the null in any frame-diversity test.

source: Schaeffer et al. (2026) Finding 10: prompt rewording raises diversity (appendix L)
finding: Gap 5. Five reworded prompts all beat the baseline prompt on embedding diversity; the anti-modal and persona phrasings aim at frame change. Temperature was fixed at 1.0, so no frame-change vs temperature comparison was made.
numbers: 12 topics, 15 models, 50 responses each, 6 phrasings. Sign tests: 25 of 30 reach the floor p=2.4e-4 (phrasing beats baseline in all 12 topics). Baseline ranks worst of six phrasings in 72% of cells. Effective rank poet_persona 17.4 to 28.9 (+66.1%) at one scale and 43.7 to 120.2 (+175.0%) at another. Rewording moved embedding metrics and modal-idea share, not the count of ideas.
quote: Rewording moves the embedding metrics and the modal-idea share, not the number
limits: Quality was not measured. The anti_modal phrasing (consider what most models would produce, then choose differently) was one of five and not separated out in the text read.
agent_relevance: Frame-change instruction beats the plain prompt for spread. Whether it beats temperature at equal quality is unmeasured. Gap 5 half closed.

finding: Gap 1 and 5. A prompt that asks the model for several answers with probabilities beats direct prompting and a sequence-of-answers prompt on diversity, and shifts the diversity-quality Pareto front relative to temperature changes.
numbers: Creative writing diversity 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting; recovers 66.8% of base-model diversity; human study 90 annotators (30 per task), diversity 1-4: poem 1.90 direct vs 2.39 VS, story 2.74 vs 3.06, joke 1.83 vs 3.01 (sequence 2.93). Temperature ablation t=0.4-1.4 on GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash: higher temperature raises diversity but lowers quality; VS gives a better Pareto front.
quote: relieves the pressure to produce a single typical answer
limits: Poems, stories, jokes; diversity is style and plot variety, not changed solution frame. No verifiable-answer task.
agent_relevance: An equal-token baseline for O8: ask for k reframings with probabilities. Strongest cheap control we have; still not a rule-change test.

source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown, Jordanous (2024) Is temperature the creativity parameter of LLMs?
finding: Gap 1. Temperature has only a weak link to novelty, a moderate link to incoherence and none to cohesion or typicality in story generation.
numbers: Fixed model and prompt; stories rated on novelty, typicality, cohesion, coherence. Weak positive correlation with novelty, moderate negative with coherence. Exact r values not extracted.
limits: One model, one narrative prompt, human raters, small scale. No code-checkable task.
agent_relevance: A temperature sweep is a weak control and easy to beat. The control that matters is the verbalized-sampling or best-of-N baseline.

source: Qian et al. (2025) EscapeBench: EscapeAgent ablation (Table 7)
finding: Gap 9. Foresight (propose and check tool-use ideas) plus Reflection (task list) cut hints and steps against the base agent, and each alone gives about half the gain. No replication on another environment and no token accounting.
numbers: 36 game settings, temperature 0. GPT-4o: hints 9.83 to 5.00 (-49%), steps 707 to 452 (-36%) [row order partly garbled in the extracted text, base row inferred]; Foresight only 6.75 / 570. Llama-3.1-70B: hints 14.67 to 7.17, steps 981 to 625; Reflection only 11.33, Foresight only 11.00.
quote: Reflection alone often outperforms Foresight alone
limits: Design and test on the same benchmark; extra modules add LLM calls (not counted); no seeds or intervals found; agent still far from humans.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 stays open. A propose-then-check step helps here; needs a token-matched rerun on another game suite.

source: Bhushan et al. (2026) agent creativity on ML engineering: search policy and decoupling
finding: Gap 7. Different search policies (greedy, MCTS, evolutionary) converge to the same low P-creativity within a few episodes, and the change in novelty is unrelated to the change in score. Nobody tested an impasse detector.
numbers: Episode-to-episode Spearman between change in impact and change in P-creativity: Human -0.111 (p<0.05), AIDE GPT-5 -0.021, AIDE Qwen3-32B 0.056, AIRA Qwen3-32B -0.026. GPT-5 H-creativity 1.423 vs gold-medal humans 0.744; only 21.25% of GPT-5 runs and 10.85% of Qwen3-32B runs reach medal level. Case: novel paradigm, refines, then stuck 6 episodes.
quote: search policy is not the binding constraint
limits: P-creativity is relative to the agent's own history. COLM 2026 paper, one group. No intervention arm.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open. The scaffold, not the search policy, drives behaviour; an impasse trigger (G1) is the missing intervention and needs its own run.

source: Schapiro, Black, Varshney (2025) Transformational creativity in science: Theorem 4 (full proof re-read)
finding: Gap 6. The edit-the-most-upstream-axiom-first result is a counting fact about dependency DAGs. It says an axiom has at least as many dependents as any rule; it says nothing about whether the edited space still gives valid or useful solutions.
numbers: Transformative potential is defined as the number of dependents. Proof: if a non-axiom R has a parent u, then |depends(u)| >= |depends(R)|+1, so the max must be an axiom. Three historical illustrations (heliocentrism, relativity, non-Euclidean geometry). No experiment.
limits: True by construction. Real constraint sets are not clean DAGs; large impact may be breakage, not progress.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 stays open. A real test needs a constraint-relaxation task with a checker: compare valid-solution yield for high-dependency vs random edits. Baba Is AI (d06) could host it.

source: Search status for rule-change benchmarks 2024-2026 (this session)
finding: Gap 8. Baba Is AI is the one verifiable rule-change benchmark found. TwistBench and Spark could not be retrieved: arXiv API, arXiv search, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned HTTP 429, and the shared WebSearch budget ran out after one call, which returned only Baba Is AI and RULEBREAKERS (logic vs world knowledge, ICML 2025).
numbers: One WebSearch answered; others hit the budget limit.
limits: Absence of other hits is a search failure, not proof none exist.
agent_relevance: Treat Gap 8 as partly closed (Baba Is AI); keep TwistBench and Spark as to-do.

source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani (2025) T-UoT human results on narrow tasks (Table 1, D.2)
finding: Gap 1. T-UoT with GPT-4o beat other GPT-4o reasoning methods on two of three narrow tasks, and beat single-prompt GPT-5 on four of six task-evaluator cells, but the wins sit on low-constraint tasks with 10 generations per cell.
numbers: Bridge human creativity 0.680 (T-UoT); LLM-rated Bridge 0.698, Electricity 0.526. T-UoT beats GPT-5 on 4 of 6 task-evaluator comparisons and DeepSeek V3.1 on 3 of 6; frontier models lead on the ambiguous Society task. 10 independent solutions per method.
limits: No intervals; the GPT-5 comparison is a single task prompt, not a matched backbone.
agent_relevance: Rule-change scaffolds can help weaker models on narrow low-constraint problems; no evidence on frontier models with code checks.
